status: Fixed in source; frozen publication pending
area: Lane refusal does not disclose the owner lane it is comparing against
finding: ATM_LANE_BORROWED_ACTOR_BLOCKED refuses a governed mutation when the executing lane is not the owner lane, but the message names neither the owner lane it expected nor where that value is recorded. The owner lane is already in the caller's hands: the ledger claim carries claim.laneSession.laneSessionId together with an exportHint that is the exact command needed to proceed. An actor that has minted more than one lane session in a session therefore has no way to tell which of them is authoritative except by guessing, and guessing across lanes is exactly the shape of probing a governed gate that the framework otherwise forbids.
expectedBehavior: A refusal must disclose the record that decided it. The lane refusal should report the ledger path it read the owner claim from, whether that claim records a lane and an export hint, and a command that reads it. It must not disclose the lane value itself under any condition — --actor is attribution, not authority, so a rule of the form 'reveal the hint when the caller presents the owner actor string' would hand the capability to precisely the borrowed-actor attempt the gate exists to stop. Location is safe because the ledger is already readable by anyone holding the repository; the capability is not.
evidenceOrRepro: ATM-GOV-0365, whose delivery landed as 642d7382b. taskflow close --write refused twice: once with no lane (ATM_LANE_BORROWED_ACTOR_BLOCKED, no executing lane capability) and once under lane-20260813155237-claude-008-gov-0365-c080ef9223 (executing lane does not match the owner lane capability). Three lane sessions existed for the same actor. The authoritative one, lane-20260813154659-claude-008-gov-0365-cc1e754c97, was recorded in .atm/history/tasks/ATM-GOV-0365.json under claim.laneSession, together with its own exportHint. Reading the ledger resolved the block in one step; the refusal that had been paid twice never pointed there. Close then succeeded and sealed as 1f2674a50.
followUp: Fixed in source by ATM-GOV-0366. authorizeLaneCapability now attaches describeOwnerLaneSource to the refusal details: schema atm.laneCapabilityRefusalDisclosure.v1, carrying ownerClaimPath, ownerLaneRecorded, ownerLaneExportHintRecorded and a nextCommand that reads that record. The first draft of this item proposed disclosing the claim's exportHint to a caller whose --actor matched the owner actor; writing the test refuted it, because that caller is the borrowed-actor attempt by definition. The disclosure is therefore identical for every attempt and contains no lane value, which the regression asserts directly. Gate behaviour is unchanged; allowed stays false. The description is derived from the claim evaluateLaneCapability already read and is carried on the decision, so the refusal reports the source it consulted rather than reopening the ledger to describe itself — INV-ATM-012 at its smallest scale. Regression guard: test_atm_gov_0366_refusal_discloses_the_owner_lane_source in tests/cli/borrowed-actor-authority-hard-gate.test.ts, which also re-asserts that neither the owner lane key nor the owner lease appears in the thrown payload. The frozen runner still carries the old refusal, so this joins the pending publication batch with [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-013], [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-015], [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-019] and [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-020]. Related to [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-017], which covers the deeper defect that claim identity is not atomic across the ledger, runtime lock and direction lock; this item is the cheap disclosure half of it and can be fixed independently. Closing ATM-GOV-0366 produced fresh evidence for that item: tasks import --write --force preserved the claim, its lease id and its lane session — the ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-008 fix confirmed live in the frozen runner — yet the ledger came back with no workAdmissionTicket key, so the next governed commit failed ATM_WORK_ADMISSION_DELIVERY_NOT_AUTHORIZED. Two things are worth carrying into that item's fix. The refusal read as an identity mismatch although the ledger held no ticket at all, which points at the mismatch and missing branches not being distinguishable to the caller; and tasks renew is the governed reseal that recovers it, which is not named by the refusal. Neither observation was reduced to a mechanism here. A separate observation from the same close, not yet reduced to a cause and therefore not claimed here: the first close attempt under the correct lane reported ATM_TASKFLOW_CLOSE_WRITE_ROLLED_BACK after its backend reported ATM_TASKS_CLOSED, and an identical second invocation succeeded. If that recurs, capture both payloads before retrying — a write path whose second attempt succeeds is either correctly idempotent or silently order-dependent, and the two are not distinguishable from a single success.
